name: InVariant
description: Infrastructure intelligence platform, being built as a startup. A Playwright agent intercepts live network traffic to fingerprint a company's stack and generates shareable security reports. Call graph engine with 9 node types, 10 edge types and 13 cross-component analyses (tree-sitter + Python AST), streamed over SSE. An LLM agent tries to disprove each finding before it's surfaced. Validated with 12 founders.

deepdive.tagline: Infrastructure intelligence: reads your code and your live stack together, and argues with its own findings before showing them.
deepdive.overview: Invariant is an infrastructure intelligence platform I'm building as a startup. It combines a static call-graph engine, a live Playwright agent that watches real network traffic, a Rust CLI, and a web app, so code-level and runtime signals end up in one place.
deepdive.why: Security auditing is largely manual — expensive, slow, and inconsistent. InVariant automates the reconnaissance and analysis phase while being smart enough to know what to look for based on what it discovers. The autonomous agent doesn't run a checklist; it reasons about what to investigate next.

components.name: Stack Fingerprinting Agent
components.description: Intercepts live network traffic to fingerprint a company's full stack, then generates shareable outbound security reports.

components.name: Call Graph Engine
components.description: 9 node types, 10 edge types and 13 cross-component analyses, streamed to the client over SSE.

components.name: Adversarial Verification
components.description: Before a finding is surfaced, an LLM agent tries to disprove it. Findings that don't survive get dropped.

components.name: Rust CLI
components.description: Offline-capable session-replay scanning with device-flow auth, for environments that can't send data to a cloud service.

components.name: Graph Visualization
components.description: Force-directed graph with 300-tick pre-settlement and 3 zoom levels; switches to Canvas above 800 nodes.

metrics: 9 node types · 10 edge types · 13 cross-component analyses
Validated with 12 founders
Canvas rendering above 800 nodes

name: HippoVoice
description: Long-term memory for voice AI companions: Ebbinghaus-style decay with per-emotion salience, a semantic/episodic split, and HippoRAG-style graph retrieval (vector + BM25 seeds, 1-hop graph walk). Benchmarked on LoCoMo (1,540 QA pairs) against local Mem0/A-MEM reimplementations on the same harness. Runs end-to-end behind Qwen2.5-Omni audio-to-audio.

deepdive.tagline: Memory that behaves less like a vector database and more like a person: things fade unless they matter or get recalled again.
deepdive.overview: HippoVoice is a memory system for voice AI companions built on two ideas from how human memory works: Ebbinghaus-style decay and HippoRAG-style associative retrieval. It started as a research demo for Rumik. Every baseline is a local reimplementation run through one harness, because published Mem0/Zep LoCoMo numbers use different LLMs and lenient LLM-as-judge scoring.
deepdive.why: Standard RAG retrieves by similarity and keeps everything forever. That's fine on a small benchmark and gets worse as a store grows for months. I wanted retrieval that stays clean as memory piles up, and a measurement setup honest enough to tell me whether it actually does.

components.name: Decay + Emotion Salience
components.description: Ebbinghaus forgetting curves with per-emotion decay multipliers. Salience drops over turns unless something boosts it.

components.name: Graph Retrieval
components.description: HippoRAG-style: vector and BM25 keyword seeds, then a 1-hop graph walk, blending relevance with log-normalized salience.

components.name: Fair Baselines
components.description: Mem0-style, A-MEM-style and Zep-style baselines on identical infrastructure and LoCoMo's published token-F1 scorer.

components.name: Voice Pipeline
components.description: The same memory runs behind an audio-to-audio model: a fact stated in one spoken turn is recalled correctly after an unrelated turn in between.

metrics: LoCoMo, 1,540 QA pairs: 29.47% avg F1 vs 29.11% Mem0-style at matched top_k=10 (a tie)
Synthetic contamination benchmark: 10% irrelevant context retrieved vs 30% for Mem0-style and flat RAG
Audio-to-audio (Qwen2.5-Omni): 25.81% avg F1 on a 40-question run, zero errors
Early 'lead' traced to a top_k mismatch and corrected; documented in BUGS.md

name: QuantEdge
description: Rust quant research platform, run daily. Multi-factor stock picker (momentum, fundamentals z-scored within GICS sector, SEC Form 4 insider activity, macro), a backtester with a real cost model, and a hash-chained, append-only forward-test log that records each day's picks before their holding-period outcomes are known. Natural-language strategies parsed by Gemini. Supports NSE and US markets.

deepdive.tagline: A quant research stack built around one rule: the only honest evidence is a prediction logged before you know if it was right.
deepdive.overview: QuantEdge is a Rust quant research platform: a point-in-time data layer, a multi-factor stock picker, a backtester, and a tamper-evident forward-test log. Most of the design effort goes into making look-ahead bias structurally impossible and making the log impossible to quietly edit.
deepdive.why: Most retail quant tools are either too simple (no real signal construction) or require expensive Bloomberg terminals. I built what I actually wanted to use: a proper multi-signal scorer with natural language strategy configuration and full backtesting.

components.name: Multi-Signal Engine
components.description: Momentum, fundamentals (P/E, EPS growth z-scored within GICS sector, keyed to actual SEC filing dates), insider activity (SEC Form 4) and macro (VIX, yield curve). GDELT and Reddit sentiment were tested live and switched off rather than shipped as fake signals.

components.name: Natural Language Strategy Input
components.description: Strategy weights specified in natural language — 'weight momentum 2x, ignore insider activity for tech stocks' — parsed by Gemini into signal weight vectors. No config files to edit.

components.name: Backtesting Engine
components.description: Next-open fills, spread/slippage/square-root market impact cost model, rank-IC signal validation, drawdown circuit breaker, beta/VaR/CVaR reporting. An AsOf view can't return data dated after its as-of date, enforced in SQL and again in Rust.

components.name: Forward-Test Log
components.description: A GitHub Actions workflow logs the model's picks every trading day, before their holding-period outcomes are known. Each entry stores the hash of the one before it, so editing or deleting a past entry breaks the chain.

components.name: Paper Portfolio
components.description: Persistent paper portfolio with daily P&L tracking and rebalance alerts. All data cached locally in SQLite for offline operation and fast backtests.

metrics: NSE and US markets (live universe: 318 US stocks)
Hash-chained forward-test log, appended daily by CI
194 Rust tests, clippy in CI
Point-in-time fundamentals and S&P 500 membership
Backtests: Sharpe, max drawdown, VaR/CVaR, rank-IC

name: WTP Dynamic Pricing
description: Real-time checkout personalization layer for Indian e-commerce, sitting between a merchant's checkout and Razorpay. Estimates willingness-to-pay from behavioral signals and adjusts price and offer in under 200ms. LightGBM WTP regressor (R² ≈ 0.91) and conversion classifier (AUC ≈ 0.72), SHAP-explained decisions, and guardrails so low-trust buyers never pay above list. Razorpay Buildathon 2026, Track 01.

name: VaultScope
description: AI-powered IPsec VPN protocol analyzer for SIH 2026 (SIH26160, NTRO), built as a team. I built most of the analysis core: the IKEv1/v2 parser that reconstructs each session's crypto negotiation, the ingestion and ESP flow-feature stages, the protocol and traffic-type classifiers, and part of the CVE-linked rules engine. On the team's 300-capture dataset (6 traffic classes), the traffic classifier went from 0.79 to 0.98 macro-F1.

name: Cash Flow Oracle
description: Settlement forecasting for merchants: GARCH(1,1) + HMM regime detection + Prophet for 30–60 day projections with confidence intervals, plus credit recommendations and stress-period detection. Razorpay Buildathon 2026, Track 04.

name: Synthetic Market RL
description: Synthetic financial market environment for LLM agent evaluation. Uses GARCH(1,1) volatility clustering and Hidden Markov regime switching — simulates dynamics rather than replaying data, making lookahead bias structurally impossible. Three difficulty tiers, 50+ news headline templates via Poisson shocks, FastAPI server, Docker deployment.

deepdive.tagline: Synthetic financial market environment that simulates dynamics rather than replaying history — lookahead bias is structurally impossible.
deepdive.overview: Most backtesting environments replay historical data, which allows subtle forms of lookahead bias that aren't always obvious. I built an environment that simulates market dynamics from statistical properties instead, making lookahead bias impossible by construction.
deepdive.why: Standard backtesting environments either use historical data (lookahead risk) or oversimplify dynamics. I wanted something that could be used to honestly evaluate trading agents without the subtle leakage that makes backtest results look better than they are.

components.name: Market Engine
components.description: GARCH(1,1) volatility clustering + Hidden Markov regime switching. Simulates realistic market dynamics including volatility clusters, trend regimes, and mean reversion. Because it simulates rather than replays, lookahead bias is structurally impossible.

components.name: Three Difficulty Tiers
components.description: Tier 1: Single-asset trend following. Tier 2: Dual-asset regime navigation with guaranteed regime switches. Tier 3: Four-asset portfolio-under-stress with hard drawdown termination.

components.name: News Shock System
components.description: 50+ headline templates with Poisson-timed delivery. Cholesky correlation sampling for correlated multi-asset moves during news events.

components.name: Deployment
components.description: FastAPI REST server with full Docker deployment for easy reproduction. Full validation suite to ensure environment correctness across all tiers.

metrics: GARCH(1,1) + HMM regime switching
3 difficulty tiers with distinct market regimes
50+ news headline templates with Poisson timing
Cholesky correlation sampling for multi-asset correlation
Lookahead bias structurally impossible by design

name: ChainedThought
description: Multi-agent deep research system built in late 2024 — predates and mirrors what commercial 'deep research' products now do. Takes a complex query, spins up N specialized sub-agents (economics, funding, startups, technology, etc.), each researches from their domain perspective. Orchestrator synthesizes all perspectives into structured output.

deepdive.tagline: Multi-agent deep research system built before commercial deep research products existed — specialized sub-agents plus orchestrated synthesis.
deepdive.overview: Built in late 2024, ChainedThought implements the multi-agent research pattern: spin up domain-specialized sub-agents, let each research from their perspective, orchestrate synthesis. This pattern is now the standard architecture for 'deep research' products. ChainedThought was built before that pattern became mainstream.
deepdive.why: Deep research on a complex question requires multiple perspectives — economics, technology, market, regulatory. A single-agent system optimizes for one perspective and misses the rest. Built in late 2024, before OpenAI and Perplexity shipped similar products in early 2025.

components.name: Query Decomposition
components.description: Takes a complex query and decomposes it into domain-specific research questions. Spawns N specialized sub-agents — economics, funding, startups, technology, regulatory, etc.

components.name: Specialized Sub-Agents
components.description: Each agent researches from their domain perspective with different priors, different tool access, and different evaluation criteria. They disagree by design — that's the point.

components.name: Orchestrator Agent
components.description: Synthesizes all sub-agent perspectives into a final structured output. Identifies agreements, contradictions, and gaps across domain perspectives. The disagreements are as informative as the agreements.

metrics: Built Nov 2024 — before commercial deep research launched
N specialized sub-agents per query
Domain-specific agent priors and tool access
Structured synthesis with explicit contradiction tracking

name: BuildFlow
description: AI-assisted project management platform serving 200+ enterprise users with 500+ active projects. Guides teams from idea to shipped product: AI-assisted ideation with retained context, feature refinement for MVP scoping, personalized task generation, Kanban tracking, Sonar API research. Multi-tenant, 99.9% uptime.

deepdive.tagline: AI-assisted project management — from ambiguous idea to shipped product, with 200+ enterprise users and 99.9% uptime.
deepdive.overview: BuildFlow is an end-to-end project management platform with AI assistance at each stage of the product lifecycle. Unlike generic PM tools, it's designed specifically to take projects from ambiguous initial idea all the way to shipped product.
deepdive.why: Most PM tools assume you know what to build. LLMs lose context of your product between sessions, requiring constant re-explanation. BuildFlow maintains persistent product context and helps you figure out what to build before helping you build it.

components.name: AI-Assisted Ideation
components.description: Context-aware ideation with retained context across sessions. The AI knows the project history and avoids suggesting things already tried.

components.name: MVP Scoping
components.description: Feature refinement for MVP scope. Helps teams distinguish core from nice-to-have. Generates prioritized feature lists based on impact/effort. Integrates Sonar API for market and competitive research.

components.name: Personalized Task Generation
components.description: Task generation calibrated to team experience level. A task list for a senior engineer looks different from one for a junior — different granularity, different assumptions.

components.name: Infrastructure
components.description: Role-based access control, multi-tenant architecture, automated CI/CD with zero-downtime deployments. Public project showcase for sharing with recruiters and investors.

metrics: 200+ enterprise users
500+ active projects
99.9% uptime with zero-downtime deployments
Multi-tenant architecture with RBAC
Public project showcase integrated

name: SNUXplore
description: Campus platform for Shiv Nadar University, built with a team of 5 and now on v4. Scaled to 30,000+ concurrent users via distributed architecture with load balancing, multi-layer caching, and optimized queries for sub-100ms response times. RAG-based LLM for natural-language queries across campus data.

deepdive.tagline: Campus platform for 30,000+ concurrent users with sub-100ms response times and RAG-based natural language queries.
deepdive.overview: SNUXplore is a campus platform for Shiv Nadar University. What started as a course planner grew into a full campus intelligence system. The scale story is the interesting part — 30,000+ concurrent users during course registration periods when everyone hits the system in the same five-minute window.
deepdive.why: SNU's existing tools were fragmented and slow. Students couldn't easily find which courses were available, which professors taught what, or how to plan their degree. The 30K concurrent users in the first week proved the pain point was real.

components.name: Distributed Architecture
components.description: Distributed architecture with load balancing and multi-layer caching. Designed for sudden traffic spikes during course registration — everyone trying to enroll in the same five-minute window.

components.name: RAG Query System
components.description: RAG-based LLM system for intelligent natural-language query resolution. Students can ask 'which professor's CS electives have the best peer ratings' and get accurate, sourced answers.

components.name: Performance Layer
components.description: Optimized queries achieving sub-100ms response times at 30K+ concurrent users. CDN, application, and database caching tiers working in concert.

metrics: 30,000+ concurrent users
Sub-100ms response times under peak load
Distributed architecture with multi-layer caching
RAG-based natural language query system
Live: snu-xplore-six.vercel.app

name: PACER
description: Can epoch-based memory reclamation for lock-free data structures adapt to workload pressure? Built in C++ (a setbench drop-in extending token4, Kim et al. PPoPP '24) and Rust (with loom model-checked tests). Stress testing showed the original 10–22% speedup was a use-after-free bug; once fixed, PACER ties the baseline. The repo keeps the receipts.

deepdive.tagline: Adaptive epoch-based reclamation, tested until it either held up or didn't. It didn't, and the write-up says so.
deepdive.overview: PACER asks whether epoch-based reclamation can adapt its freeing policy to workload pressure. I implemented it twice, as a C++ reclaimer for Brown's setbench and as a from-scratch Rust core, then stress-tested and benchmarked it on Linux.
deepdive.why: The early numbers looked like a 10–22% win. I didn't trust them, so I kept stress-testing. The win turned out to be a use-after-free in my own reclaimer. Fixing it and publishing the tie is more useful than a result that crashes 6 runs out of 10.

components.name: C++ Reclaimer
components.description: Drop-in reclaimer extending token4. Freed the epoch bag still being written to: heap corruption in 6 of 10 runs at 16 threads. After the fix, 20 of 20 clean runs.

components.name: Rust Core
components.description: Tier selection with hysteresis and a snapshot-coalescing coordinator. Tests and the loom model checker caught a livelock and a torn read; both fixed with regression tests.

components.name: Backlog Instrumentation
components.description: Tracking retired-node backlog, not just throughput, exposed an unbounded leak (1.5M retired nodes vs 255 for DEBRA). Fixed with a per-op / per-window split.

metrics: After the fix: 0.93–1.03× vs token4 (a tie within noise)
Free-count sweep K ∈ {1..64}: K=1 best everywhere; K=64 cost up to 35% throughput
3 concurrency bugs found and fixed, all with regression tests
Raw CSVs behind every number in the repo

name: OS Resource Mgmt
description: Simulation of an advanced OS resource management system: Intelligent Process Scheduling with usage pattern analysis and ML-inspired dynamic priorities; Adaptive Memory Management with predictive allocation; Enhanced Security with layered protection, anomaly detection, and process trust scoring. Simulates 100–200 processes. Accompanied by IEEE paper.

name: AdvisoryAI
description: .NET engine for automated Word document template processing. Detects highlighted sections as fillable blanks, uses LLM or structured input to fill them optimally. Solves Word document automation at the template level rather than the content level. Built for a hackathon.

name: Crypto Tx Tracker
description: Cryptocurrency transaction trail analyzer. Input any transaction, trace money flow to configurable depth across the chain — surfaces whether funds from flagged transactions were eventually withdrawn or mixed. Graph-based traversal. Meaningfully novel in 2023 before this became a standard compliance tool.

name: DeBi
description: NFT launchpad for businesses to launch their own tokens — fungible or non-fungible. Positioned as a digital IPO tool. Meaningfully early in 2023 before this became standard. Smart contracts in Solidity, React frontend with Web3 integration.

name: DeLogi
description: QR code-based supply chain provenance system. Products carry a QR code scanned at every production/logistics touchpoint, creating an immutable audit trail. Built as part of CatalystIQ suite. Discontinued due to Indian market fit — the market wasn't ready.

name: Petner
description: Pet-focused social platform. First startup, started at age 16. Built across multiple iterations over two years — petnerSocial, petnerv1, petnerNext, petnerPlat. Demonstrated sustained product iteration and early entrepreneurial instinct.

name: LLM News Bias Analyzer
description: Built an LLM from scratch for news article analysis. Three functions: summarization, political perspective classification (left/right bias detection), and alternate perspective discovery via search to flag when a story has contradicting coverage elsewhere. Multi-model pipeline with retrieval augmentation.

name: NewsOCR / BookOCR
description: OCR pipeline using Tesseract for extraction, structured and cleaned by a local LLM. Cheaper than cloud OCR APIs, works well on real documents including books and news articles. The same OCR engine was reused in the Pactle quote generator for image-based RFQs.
